newsitem.title: USA: Cattlemen study privatizing US beef grading system.
newsitem.headline: Cattlemen study privatizing US beef grading system.

text.p: In hopes of improving beef grading as well as the flow of information from meat packers to cattlemen, some U.S. cattlemen suggested Friday that federal meat graders be replaced with non-government ones.

Currently, meat graders employed by the U.S. Agriculture Department inspect beef that passes through major U.S. packing plants. Some cattlemen said unless USDA improves the grading system perhaps it should be replaced with an industry-funded system.
One of the cattlemen, Ron Baker, who chairs a National Cattlemen's Beef Association subcommittee on privatization, said beef grading needs to be improved.
"They (NCBA leaders) didn't feel we were correctly identifying the quality in the beef," Baker said, referring to the existing system.

During a Friday session at the NCBA summer meeting, Baker's committee suggested USDA be encouraged to upgrade its beef grading system, and if that effort fails the NCBA should further develop its plan of using industry-funded graders.
NCBA members will review the subcommittee's proposal during meetings Saturday.

The Canadian meat packing industry in April 1996 switched to the privately-funded Canadian Beef Grading Agency. NCBA members who visited Canadian beef plants, said at Friday's NCBA session the Canadian agency had lowered grading costs, improved communication throughout the production chain, and employed modern grading technology.
